headline: Test 1: Portugal, 1441–1486 · 32:36

items.title: 32:36 · In 1441 a young Portuguese captain named
items.detail: In 1441, a young Portuguese captain named Antao Goncalves sailed to the Rio d'Ouro coast under orders from Prince Henry the Navigator to procure cargoes of sea-wolf skins and oil.

items.title: 32:48 · Seeking personal promotion and higher commercial return
items.detail: Seeking personal promotion and higher commercial return, Goncalves exceeded his commission, led an armed raiding party ashore at night, and seized two Sanhaja Berber captives to carry back to Lisbon.

items.title: 33:00 · Notice the date of that raid 1441
items.detail: Notice the date of that raid: 1441.

items.title: 33:10 · Once Prince Henry and the Lisbon court
items.detail: Once Prince Henry and the Lisbon court saw the commercial return on human cargo, the Crown moved immediately from opportunistic raiding to chartered corporate logistics.

items.title: 33:20 · In 1444 under the patronage of Prince
items.detail: In 1444, under the patronage of Prince Henry, merchants in the Algarve formed the Companhia de Lagos, a chartered joint-stock syndicate organized specifically to finance large-scale slave-raiding expeditions.
